title: Certify v0.7.0: the oriented Ramsey number k(3,4) = r(I_3, L_4) = 21 — a previously unknown value in Erdos Problem #112, determined and certified
description: Let k(n,m) be the least N such that every directed graph on N vertices contains an independent set of size n or a transitive tournament on m vertices (Erdos Problem #112; equivalently the oriented-graph Ramsey number r(I_n, L_m)). Known exact values were k(3,3) = 9 (Bermond 1974) and k(4,3) = 15, k(5,3) = 23 (Ihringer-Rajendraprasad-Weinert 2021); the published bounds for k(3,4) were 9 <= k(3,4) <= 25. This release determines k(3,4) = 21: an explicit 20-vertex oriented graph containing neither pattern (checkable in milliseconds by the shipped standard-library verifier), together with an exhaustion of the 21-vertex case via a neighbourhood decomposition into 346 propositional instances, each refuted by CaDiCaL with an LRAT certificate and every certificate replayed by an independently written standard-library checker; completeness of the decomposition was audited at clause-multiset level against independent re-derivations, and redundant confirming exhaustions were run at 22, 23 and 24 vertices (445 certificates, ~1.02e9 checked proof steps; certificates regenerate bit-for-bit from recorded solver commands, 11/11 attempts). From the same campaign: 29 <= k(6,3) <= 33, the lower bound new via the vertex-transitive witness Cay(Z_28, {3,8,10,12,17}) (independence number exactly 5, no transitive triangle; separately refereed), the upper bound due to IRW. The from-definition CNF generator ships with the release, so the entire chain is reproducible without trusting the authors' encodings. Every component was confirmed by an adversarial referee writing fresh code throughout; review logs and dated novelty sweeps ship with the release. Computations carried out with Claude (Anthropic), directed by the author.
